title: Fair Measure
logline: At a weekly market, one vendor's old balance scales are the only ones nobody double-checks, and a neighbouring stallholder's quiet suggestion to shave a little weight off gets a flat no.

object.note: Object 6 (identity not chosen) may appear subtly, for example among Chathura's things while he travels, waits or watches, only where it sits naturally in a real moment. Never staged, never the subject.

thread_in.thread: Giving without keeping count becomes weighing honestly when no one checks: a market vendor whose old scales nobody doubts.

thread_out.thread: From an honest scale at a weekly market to the weighing on a fishing beach, where one boat's big catch meets the others' light ones and the next ten minutes say more than the scale.

requirements: A weekly market with an established, trusted vendor willing to be filmed
A real, observed moment rather than a recreated or hypothetical one
Cooperation from neighbouring stallholders and market organisers

lesson.in_simple_terms: Being honest is not only a background trait. The texts describe a specific good moment that happens when a person has a real chance to cheat and turns it down.
lesson.in_simple_terms_si: අභිධර්මයට අනුව, වංචා කිරීමට සැබෑ අවස්ථාවක් ආ විට එය නොකර සිටින මොහොතේ, වැළකීම නම් වූ විශේෂ යහපත් ගුණයක් සිතේ පහළ වේ.
lesson.the_teaching: Among the beautiful mental factors that arise only when conditions call for them are three abstinences, one of which is right livelihood: refraining from wrong conduct done to earn a living. The Pradeepika says that simply running a blameless trade is not this abstinence; it exists only when a wrong way of earning is actually refused. In ordinary good minds, the texts say, an abstinence arises occasionally and one at a time, only in the moment a particular wrong is being held back from. The Margaya adds that a person can stop in the moment, with no earlier vow, simply by seeing the fault in the wrong.
lesson.how_the_film_shows_it: Most of the film is the unremarkable rhythm of trade: scales, weights, banter, a customer double-checking a weighing at another stall. Inside that rhythm comes one small, real test, the neighbour's quiet suggestion to shave a little weight, and the flat no. The viewer sees that the old scales nobody doubts rest on moments exactly like this one.

key_terms.en: abstinence; actively refraining from a wrong one could do
right livelihood: refraining from wrong conduct done to earn a living
abstinence in the moment, without an earlier vow

lesson.caution: This does not mean that simply having an honest trade is the virtue; the texts place right livelihood in the actual refusal of a wrong way of earning.
lesson.builds_on: The free table showed goodness as giving without keeping count; this film shows goodness that consists of not doing something, weighing honestly when no one would check.
